title: The Update
focus: 及早报告阻塞，并提供事实和下一步
story:
The waiting circle turns for so long that I begin to watch it instead of the clock. Then the request fails. I try again with the same test account, and the same red message appears.

It is several weeks after the staff demonstration. We have changed the notification layout and collected more questions from the centres. Now I am connecting our work to the client's test service, which provides enrolment information.

Without that information, we cannot reliably check who should receive a changed-time email.

Beside my keyboard is a page from the staff demonstration. At the top I have written a question from the woman who answered an imaginary phone: How do you know you have the right list?

This morning Mei offered to sit with me and compare the two lists once the connection was ready. She set aside the hour before lunch. At eleven thirty she came over carrying a banana and her notebook.

“Still a good time?”

“Give me ten minutes.”

She peeled the banana. We watched the circle turn. By the time she dropped the skin into the bin, I was back at the same red message.

“I have to go,” she said. “Someone needs me to look at the calendar. Tell me when you've got something I can compare.”

Now the empty chair beside me is bothering me more than the red message. She could have spent that half hour somewhere else.

Yesterday, I thought the connection problem would take an hour. This morning, I thought it would be fixed before lunch. It is now two fifteen. Our team update starts at three.

I open the request details again. Access denied. Perhaps I have missed something obvious. Perhaps everyone else would know what to change.

Rui rolls his chair back. “Coming for coffee?”

“In a minute.”

“You said that an hour ago.”

“I need to fix this first.”

He looks at the screen. “How long has it been blocked?”

“Since yesterday afternoon.”

“Does Daniel know?”

“He knows I'm working on the connection.”

“That isn't the same thing.”

The words annoy me because they are true. I turn towards him.

“I don't want to report a problem I should be able to solve.”

Rui puts his mug down. “Report what you've checked. Then we can decide whether it's yours to solve.”

We spend ten minutes comparing the request with the client's instructions. The address is correct. The account name is correct. A basic connection succeeds, but the enrolment request is refused. I have enough facts to describe the problem, even if I do not have its answer.

I send Daniel a short message before the update. He replies, 'Bring that first.'

At three, five of us gather around a table. Daniel opens a list of tasks. My name is halfway down, but he looks at me immediately.

“What's blocking the connection?”

“The client test service refuses our enrolment request. I've checked the address and account details. The basic connection works, so the service is reachable.”

“What's the impact?”

“We can continue testing the screen with local data. We can't verify the full journey with the client's test records.”

“Can you finish tomorrow?”

I press my thumb against the edge of my notebook.

“I can finish my checks tomorrow. I can't promise the connection will work until we know why access is refused.”

Daniel looks unhappy. “I told Elena we'd have an update this week.”

“We can give her an update,” Rui says. “We just can't call the full test complete.”

Daniel turns back to me. “What do you need?”

“A contact who can check the account permissions. And someone to confirm which test classes we are allowed to use.”

He writes both items down. “I'll ask Elena for the right contact today. You send the facts, without passwords or keys.”

I nod. Then I add something I would rather leave out.

“I should have raised it yesterday. I kept expecting the next attempt to work.”

“Yes,” Daniel says. “Next time, tell me sooner. Waiting doesn't make the dependency smaller.”

There is no angry speech. We move to another person's task. I feel exposed for several minutes, and then strangely able to work again.

Afterwards, I prepare a short note with the failed request time, the error message and the checks already completed. I remove account secrets before sharing it. I also list what we can still test locally.

Elena replies before I leave. She gives us a service contact, but that person cannot inspect the permissions until the next day. It is not the quick rescue I hoped for.

Daniel asks me to adjust the task estimate and mark the external dependency. We agree on another update tomorrow at four, even if the problem remains unresolved.

At home, Maya is listening to a recording through headphones. She holds up one finger when I come in. I put my bag down and start washing rice.

A few minutes later, she joins me.

“Hard day?”

“I spent most of it wanting a better answer.”

“Did you get one?”

“Not yet. But other people know the actual question now.”

The rice slips between my fingers into the bowl. I turn off the tap before the water reaches the top.

The next afternoon at four I still cannot open the records. I call Mei first. I owe her at least that much.

“Have you kept another hour for me?” I ask.

“No. Should I have?”

“Good. No. The person on the client side is checking which classes the account can see. I'll ask for your time when there's a list in front of me.”

“Andy?”

“Yes?”

“Yesterday I wasn't sitting there because I thought you were slow. You said ten minutes. I believed you.”

There is no answer I can give that will give her the time back. “I know. I'm sorry.”

“Okay. Send me a picture of that list when you get it. A picture of test names,” she adds. “You can keep the red circle.”

At five past four, Daniel has my update and Mei is at somebody else's desk. The chair beside me stays empty. Today that feels right.

phrases.en: We can continue with local data.
I can’t promise that until we know the cause.
I should have raised this sooner.

practice.grammar: 用 until 说明承诺的边界：I can’t promise the connection will work until we know the cause. 再用一个 until 句说明你工作中必须先满足的条件。
practice.pronunciation: 用三段意群练习汇报：The service is reachable. / The enrolment request is refused. / We need a permissions check. 句间停顿，重读 reachable、refused、permissions。

questions.q: What works even though the enrolment request fails?
questions.a: The basic connection to the client test service works.

questions.q: What did Mei lose while Andy expected a quick fix?
questions.a: She lost time she could have spent reviewing other work.

questions.q: When will Andy provide another update?
questions.a: He will provide another update at four the next day, even if the problem is unresolved.

roleplay.context: 你是 Andy，必须在例会报告一个尚未解决的外部依赖。

turns.cue: 说清基本连接成功，但读取报名信息被拒绝。

turns.line: Can you promise it will work tomorrow?
turns.cue: 区分可以完成的排查与无法承诺的外部结果。

turns.line: What do you need from me?
turns.cue: 请求权限联系人和允许使用的测试班级信息。

practice.transfer: 你帮朋友准备活动，但场地方尚未确认座位数。用英语做四十秒进度汇报，包含事实、影响、可继续的工作和下一次更新时间。
practice.retell: 按“卡在哪里—已检查什么—影响什么—需要谁帮助—何时再更新”脱稿汇报本章，不必复述所有家庭对话。
